Class IuJsonbValueAdapter<T>

java.lang.Object
iu.client.jsonb.IuJsonbValueAdapter<T>
Type Parameters:
T - Java type
All Implemented Interfaces:
IuJsonAdapter<T>
final class IuJsonbValueAdapter<T> extends Object implements IuJsonAdapter<T>
Converts one Java type according to IuJsonb configuration.

Every nested type, including a collection item, map value, array component, or Optional value, resolves back through IuJsonb.adapt(Type), so configuration applies at any depth in both tree and streaming conversion. Precedence, for a value:

  1. The most specific configured component: a JsonbAdapter, which converts to and from its adapted type, or a JsonbSerializer or JsonbDeserializer. Between a serializer or deserializer and an adapter registered for types neither more specific than the other, such as the same type, the serializer or deserializer runs, as in Yasson. Each adapter applies at most once to a value: the adapted value converts through its type's components, less the adapters already applied, so an adapter can't loop through its own output.
  2. The built-in conversion for the declared type: IuJsonbEnumAdapter for an enum, IuJsonbAdapter for a non-platform business object, otherwise JsonAdapters.adapt(Type, java.util.function.Function).

Components form one chain per direction, most specific first; see IuJsonb. So a deserializer registered for a type reads it ahead of an adapter registered for a supertype, which can't be expected to read a value of the subtype. Writing selects components by the value's runtime type, so the order is the same wherever the value is declared, while the built-in conversion stays with the declared type. Reading skips an adapter whose adapted type doesn't accept the shape of the JSON value (string, number, boolean, object, or array), and uses the first adapter skipped if no other component runs, so adapters can accept several formats. Components registered for a broad type, such as Object, are left out of the chain for a scalar type, null included, and so for a value written with a scalar runtime type; they are also left out when reading a JSON string, number, or boolean as any type.

A serializer or deserializer passes control down its chain by passing the same value, or the parser at the same position, back to its context: the next component not already in progress for it runs, and then the built-in conversion. Since a component registered for a supertype may read a value of another subtype, what an adapter or deserializer reads is checked against the type being read, and a value that doesn't fit fails the conversion.

Null reaches user code like any other value: an adapter adapts it in both directions, a serializer is given it, and a deserializer is given a parser at VALUE_NULL. An undefined value, converted from a null JsonValue in tree mode, has no parser event, so it bypasses deserializers.

Each conversion joins the call in progress on the current thread, or starts one, so a tree conversion nested in a streaming call shares its options snapshot, property path, and cycle checks.

  • Method Details

    • accepts

      static boolean accepts(Type adapted, JsonValue.ValueType shape)
      Determines if an adapted type reads a JSON value of a given shape.

      Judged from the type alone: a number type reads numbers, a map or business object reads objects, an array or collection type reads arrays, an enum reads text or objects, and other platform types, such as text, dates, and URIs, read text. Object and JSON-P types read anything.

      Parameters:
      adapted - adapted type
      shape - JSON value type
      Returns:
      true if adapted reads values of that shape

    • read

      public T read(JsonParser parser)
      Description copied from interface: IuJsonAdapter
      Reads a JSON value from a parser and converts it to its Java equivalent.

      parser must be positioned at the value's first event: START_OBJECT, START_ARRAY, or a scalar value event. On return, parser is positioned at the value's last event: the matching END_OBJECT or END_ARRAY, or the scalar value event itself. This is the contract of JsonParser.getValue(), which the default implementation delegates to.

      Specified by:
      read in interface IuJsonAdapter<T>
      Parameters:
      parser - JSON parser
      Returns:
      Java equivalent

    • nullProperty

      JsonValue nullProperty(IuSerializationContext context, List<IuJsonb.AdapterReference> applied)
      Converts a null property value when null properties are omitted.

      Only an adapter is consulted. When it adapts the null to a value, that value converts through the adapted type; when it adapts the null to null, the adapted type's own adapters are consulted in turn.

      Parameters:
      context - call in progress
      applied - adapters already applied
      Returns:
      JSON value to include; null to omit the property
